questions.question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:

options.text: Take quick glances at the mirrors.
Look at the mirrors for a long time.
Use only the rearview mirror.
Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take quick glances at the mirrors.
questions.explanation: Looking at mirrors for too long is dangerous. You will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice.
Always be done in the same order.
Only be done on sunny days.
Not be done if the vehicle seems to work well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do the pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver, you should:

options.text: Follow their vehicle closely.
Try to get their attention.
Stay far away from them.
Flash your lights at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from them.
questions.explanation: Give a distracted driver plenty of space. Be careful when passing because the driver may not see you and could drift into your lane.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?

options.text: Green
Orange
Red
Purple

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light is red. It is found in vehicles with air brakes and may have a buzzer sound with it.

questions.question: If you must write a vehicle inspection report, you must sign it:

options.text: Every day.
Only if problems were found and fixed.
Only if repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only if a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if problems were found and fixed.
questions.explanation: Sign the previous inspection report only if problems were found and then fixed.

questions.question: If a vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, the driver should:

options.text: Stay in the vehicle and try to restart it.
Get out and walk away from the tracks.
Flag down another vehicle for help pushing.
Wait in the vehicle for police to arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk away from the tracks.
questions.explanation: If stuck on railroad tracks, leave the vehicle right away and get away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call that number or call 911.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you do NOT need to:

options.text: Show where the dipstick is.
Show the oil level is safe.
Show the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is, show the oil level is safe, and show the oil level is above the refill mark. You do not need to show that oil is below the refill mark.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, you can slow down by:

options.text: Shifting into a higher gear.
Shifting into a lower gear.
Finding a hill.
Letting the truck run out of gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shifting into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: If hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear to help slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking?

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Exercise.
Wait.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Tricks like coffee or cold showers do not speed this up. The only way to sober up is to wait for the alcohol to leave your body.

questions.question: For a double combination vehicle, the maximum air leakage during a static leakage test is:

options.text: 3 psi in one minute.
6 psi in one minute.
8 psi in one minute.
4 psi in one minute.

questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: In a static leakage test for a double combination vehicle with air brakes, air should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute. Faster leaking means something needs repair and the vehicle should not be driven.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes in an air brake system. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: What is a concern when transporting livestock on a trailer?

options.text: Livestock should never be transported on a trailer.
A law enforcement officer must inspect the livestock.
Livestock can move and shift weight, causing unsafe handling.
Only registered farmers can transport livestock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Livestock can move and shift weight, causing unsafe handling.
questions.explanation: Livestock can move around and shift their weight while being transported. This movement can make the trailer unsafe to handle.

questions.question: What does the three-time fail rule mean?

options.text: You must wait 30 days before retaking the exam after failing it three times.
You can never take the test again after failing it three times.
You must take a test for a different CDL class after failing three times.
You must take a class before retaking the exam after failing three times.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must wait 30 days before retaking the exam after failing it three times.
questions.explanation: If you fail any CDL test three times, you must wait 30 days from the date of the third failed test before you can take that test again.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a problem with the exhaust system?

options.text: Loose or broken exhaust pipes
Loose or broken mounting brackets
Exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts
Exhaust system parts that are not leaking

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts that are not leaking
questions.explanation: When inspecting the exhaust system, check that parts are not loose, broken, or missing. Parts must be properly mounted and should not rub against other vehicle parts.

questions.question: How can you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To prevent rolling backward when starting from a stop, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake. Use the parking brake as needed to prevent the vehicle from rolling back.

questions.question: How do you set the parking brake on newer vehicles?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to set the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid making quick changes.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Speed up.
Avoid signaling tricks to help others pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your following distance, avoid sudden moves, and do not use tricks like flashing lights to help them pass. Speeding up will only make the danger worse.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic pressure in the brakes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Downshift.
Pump the brakes.
Accelerate.
Use the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate.
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find an escape route such as an escape ramp, open field, or side street. Do not speed up.

questions.question: Which example shows poor lane usage on the driving test?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Stopping behind crosswalks
Driving in the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines and crosswalks. On roads with multiple lanes, stay in the rightmost lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Stay in the driver's lane.
Try to race the driver.
Ignore the driver's gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore the driver's gestures.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact, do not race them, and do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: Who is responsible for checking a vehicle's cargo?

options.text: The person who loaded it
The owner of the trucking company
The owner of the cargo
The driver

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver must check the cargo. Check for overloading, unbalanced weight, proper securing, and that cargo does not block your view or access to emergency equipment. The driver is always responsible for the cargo, even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: When leaving a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly.
Rush down the stairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handrail firmly.
questions.explanation: When leaving your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: Very hot temperatures can cause:

options.text: Tire failure.
A trailer to disengage.
Lights to malfunction.
Increased gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire failure.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, which increases tire pressure. High pressure can cause tire failure. Always check your tire pressure when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Shortens stopping distance.
Shortens brake response time.
Provides less control.
Provides more control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides more control.
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops your wheels from locking up during hard braking. This gives you better control. However, it does not always shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you fall behind on sleep
When you want to take a nap
Excess sleep
The amount of time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you fall behind on sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt occurs when you do not sleep enough. You can only repay this debt by sleeping more.

questions.question: A maximum safe speed sign means:

options.text: It is a suggestion; vehicles may travel faster than the posted speed.
It only applies to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
It only applies to automobiles.

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle should travel faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Are normal.
Indicate a potentially dangerous defect.
Will prevent the turn signals from working.
Pose no threat if the vehicle is only driven on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate a potentially dangerous defect.
questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps a vehicle's axles in place. Damaged suspension parts, such as leaking shock absorbers, are potentially dangerous defects.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during a vehicle inspection, what happens?

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle will be put out-of-service until it is fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is in place.
The driver will be asked to decrease the weight of the load.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will be put out-of-service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If at least one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing, the vehicle will be put out-of-service until the defect is fixed.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the side mirror on the driver's side.
Use both side mirrors.
Not use a helper.
Only use the side mirror on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors frequently when backing to see hazards behind your vehicle. Use a helper to watch your blind spots when possible.

questions.question: Which rule about turn signals is NOT good practice?

options.text: Signal early.
Signal continuously.
Skip your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
Cancel your signal after the turn is completed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip your turn signal if you think others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you plan to turn or change lanes. Signal well before the turn, signal continuously during the turn, and turn off the signal when the turn is complete. Never assume others know what you are doing.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The number of alcoholic drinks consumed
How fast the alcoholic drinks were consumed
The weight of the drinker
The temperature of the drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: The temperature of the drinks
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the person's weight.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while the vehicle is moving:

options.text: Is acceptable.
Allows air to cool the cargo.
Can tear away.
Can attract birds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tear away.
questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap in the wind. A flapping cover can tear loose and uncover the cargo. It can also block your view or the view of other drivers.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off manually.
Should not come on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: After an accident, flares must be used carefully because:

options.text: Spilled fuel on the road could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares.
Flares are expensive.
Other drivers may become confused.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the road could catch fire.
questions.explanation: After an accident, spilled fuel combined with improper flare use can start a fire.

questions.question: Texting while driving is dangerous because:

options.text: It creates both mental and physical distractions.
A message may upset the driver.
Texts may be more interesting than driving.
It is less efficient than a phone call.

questions.correctAnswerText: It creates both mental and physical distractions.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving distracts you both mentally and physically, making it very dangerous.

questions.question: Wheel rims that have been welded:

options.text: Should be placed on the front of the vehicle.
Should be placed on the rear of the vehicle.
Should be placed on dual tires.
Should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used.
questions.explanation: Welded wheels and rims are not safe to use. Replace any damaged wheels and rims.

questions.question: When using road speed to decide when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work best for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and try to match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work best for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Learn which speeds each gear can handle by reading your vehicle's manual. Watch your speedometer and shift up when you reach the top speed for the current gear.

questions.question: When should you be careful about black ice?

options.text: When it is snowing
When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground
Just after a rainstorm

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice that lets you see the road through it. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road surface looks wet.

questions.question: In very hot weather, you should check your tires often because:

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure may increase with the heat.
The tread wears down faster.
The lug nuts may loosen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with the heat.
questions.explanation: Heat causes air to expand. In very hot weather, tire air pressure can reach dangerously high levels. If this happens, stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as this could make the pressure too low once the tires cool down.

questions.question: After finishing a trip, you should:

options.text: Place the vehicle out-of-service.
Change the vehicle's oil.
Complete an after-trip inspection.
Disconnect the vehicle's battery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete an after-trip inspection.
questions.explanation: After a trip, you may be required to inspect each vehicle you drove and file a report.

questions.question: How should cargo inside a trailer be handled?

options.text: It does not need to be secured.
It should be stacked no more than three feet high.
It should be secured to prevent movement.
It should have the heaviest items on top of lighter items.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be secured to prevent movement.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be secured so it does not move while the vehicle is in transit. Cargo should be arranged to keep the vehicle's center of gravity low and balanced.

questions.question: What is a danger when a large truck swerves to avoid a hazard?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may flip over.
The truck may stay in the same lane.
Other vehicles may do the same thing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck may flip over.
questions.explanation: Swerving is often safer than stopping. You can turn away from something faster than you can stop. However, heavy trucks or trucks pulling multiple trailers can roll over when they swerve.

questions.question: How do you know if a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working when you start the engine?

options.text: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the trailer flashes three times and then stays on.
All the rear lights on the trailer flash and then shut off.
The blue light near the driver's door lights up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: Trailers with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have a yellow warning light on the left rear. If this light stays on after the engine starts, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: What is a benefit of using convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
They can replace flat mirrors.
They help you see a wider area.
They are illegal to use in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Curved, convex mirrors allow drivers to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance later to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check the tire tread depth.
Make sure the correct tire was changed.
Look for rocks in the tire tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After a tire is changed, stop after a short distance to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: What is the minimum size for hazardous materials placards?

options.text: Four inches.
Six and one-quarter inches.
Nine and three-quarter inches.
10 and three-quarter inches.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 and three-quarter inches.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be at least 10 and three-quarter inches square.

questions.question: How should you stop in an emergency?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Keep your vehicle in a straight line.
Turn your vehicle while braking.
Expect your vehicle to stop faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: During an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle in a straight line while braking, but still be able to turn if needed.

questions.question: What happens if a CMV driver refuses chemical testing when an officer asks?

options.text: The driver receives a ticket.
The driver's license is suspended for two months.
The driver's license is suspended for 12 months.
The driver is asked to drive straight home.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver's license is suspended for 12 months.
questions.explanation: Any driver who refuses chemical testing will have their license suspended for at least 12 months. This applies to all drivers, not just CMV drivers.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is acceptable?

options.text: No more than 10 degrees.
No more than 25 degrees.
No more than 50 degrees.
No more than 75 degrees.

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than 10 degrees.
questions.explanation: Steering wheel play should not be more than 10 degrees (about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel). More than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance later to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check the tire wear.
Check the windshield wiper fluid level.
Check the tire air pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After a tire is changed, stop after a short distance to make sure the lug nuts are still tight and secure.
